resources.string: Yes. Both the web and iOS apps are free, and there is no sign-up.
Yes, that is what Gildongmu is built around. All information is provided as text, so the entire flow of search, place details, and directions works with a screen reader such as VoiceOver.
Can blind users use it with a screen reader?
Yes. The interface is available in six languages including English, and place data is available in Korean and English.
Can I use it without knowing Korean?

Features that look things up by name, such as place search, station information, and directions to a destination, work anywhere in the world. Features based on your current location work only within South Korea.
Does it work outside South Korea?
Maps cannot be read by screen readers, so Gildongmu presents everything as text. For turn-by-turn driving it hands off to the Naver Map or KakaoMap apps.
Why is there no map view?
Place and address search: find places across Korea by name, street address, or postal code.
Route preview: get a text briefing of car, transit, and walking routes before you leave. Walking routes offer an option that avoids stairs.

Nearby information: real-time subway arrivals, buses, late-night pediatric clinics, barrier-free tourist sites, and pedestrian infrastructure such as audible signals, based on your current location. Some data, including bike share, cultural events, and crowd levels, covers Seoul.
Station information: facilities, first and last train times, and elevator locations for subway stations nationwide.
AI chat: ask about a place and get answers grounded in live data.
Developers: the npm packages gildongmu (CLI) and gildongmu-mcp (MCP server) expose the same data to terminals and AI agents.
iOS app: get Gildongmu on the App Store
Web: use it right away at gildongmu.dodoplanet.space, no installation needed.

Gildongmu is a navigation and place information service for South Korea. It is designed so screen reader users can complete the entire flow from search to directions in text, and it supports six languages: Korean, English, Spanish, French, Italian, and Japanese. Both the web and iOS apps are free, with no account required.

In the iOS app, the step count shown when you arrive with walking guidance and the body weight you enter in Settings are used only on your device; they are never transmitted or stored.

If you use Gildongmu\'s tools through an AI agent browser that supports WebMCP, the tool output is sent to that agent\'s provider. What is sent: your search query and results (place names, addresses, phone numbers), place information (a station\'s first and last trains, facilities, real-time arrivals, barrier-free facilities), and for directions the origin, destination and via names, the route summary and guidance sentences. Coordinates are never sent, but this information can reveal your location and movements. This works only when Gildongmu is opened in an AI agent browser that supports WebMCP. It does nothing in a regular browser, and there is no separate setting inside Gildongmu.
Web traffic is measured anonymously with Vercel Analytics. It uses no cookies and stores no information that identifies you.

In AI chat, your questions, the conversation, the place you are viewing, and your current location are sent to Google Gemini to generate answers. Questions that need a web search are also sent to Perplexity. Answers are AI-generated and may be inaccurate.
For questions about the service or this policy, email engccer@gmail.com.
Dictation in the iOS app is processed on your device, so audio never leaves it. Dictation on the web sends audio to Deepgram for transcription and does not store it afterwards.
Gildongmu works without an account and does not store personal data in any database of its own.

Your current location is used only to look up nearby places, transit, and directions in real time, and is not stored. It may appear temporarily in server infrastructure request logs while a request is processed.
Business hours shown in place details are looked up by sending the place name, coordinates, and road address to Google Places. Your current location is not sent.
Search terms are sent to search providers such as Kakao and Naver, and to Perplexity web search only when there are no place or address results.
